lens: PILOT-FIRST: shortest path to a credible end-to-end demo for a Mexican ITF/IFPE design partner, then the shortest path from each sub-project to visible value. Isolation primitives (RLS, per-tenant keys, policy snapshots, hash-chained audit) are never deferred; everything else inside a sub-project is cut to what the pilot can see.
summary: Build one Python 3.13 package (kycaml) as a modular monolith with two entrypoints (api, worker) over a single Postgres 17 database, following the foundations doc's intent (10-f00 §1) but collapsing its uv-workspace/service split for one developer. Twelve sub-projects run in sequence: P0 foundations and walking skeleton, P1 screening core (lists + LATAM matcher + tenant-private LPB), P2 risk scorecard, P3 MX KYC onboarding (first end-to-end demo, delivery-plan M2 equivalent), P4 transaction monitoring with reportable-event capture, P5 case management with four-eyes and the MX compliance committee, P6 reporting engine + Formato 41 (ROR/ROI/24h/ROIP incl. empty reports, M4 equivalent), P7 delta re-screening + MX freeze playbook, P8 KYB with ownership graph, P9 LFPIORPI aviso XML (second pack), P10 compliance calendar, P11 monitoring v2 (sync decisions, simulation), risk governance and pilot hardening. All deferred infrastructure (Kafka, Temporal, OpenSearch, Redis, ClickHouse, KMS, S3) sits behind eleven ports whose MVP adapters are Postgres tables, an in-process outbox dispatcher, a Postgres SKIP LOCKED job queue with a persisted workflow_run state machine, an in-memory screening index, a local-filesystem object store and a local key provider; each port ships a contract test suite that the later adapter must also pass. Sentinel contributes the audit chain, the name normaliser/matcher skeleton, identifier validators, the six monitoring rule kinds, the four-eyes case workflow with allowed_actions, the testcontainers test harness, the CI toolchain and the whole React console. Estimated 37 developer-weeks with an AI agent; the first end-to-end demo lands after P3 at roughly week 12.

modules.name: platform
modules.responsibility: Foundations with zero domain knowledge: config, db session with RLS context, UUIDv7, encryption types and blind indexes, policy-pack models/resolver/snapshots, unit service and calendar engine, event envelope + outbox + dispatcher, Postgres job queue + cron + WorkflowRun state machine, hash-chained audit, object store, connector SDK + sandbox mock framework, webhooks, clock, FastAPI conventions (API keys, staff auth, idempotency, problem+json, pagination). Owns all port interfaces and their MVP adapters.

modules.name: core
modules.responsibility: Shared tenant-scoped domain: tenant/tenant_policy/tenant_key/staff_user/api_client, party/person/organization/party_identifier/party_address/party_relationship, document, verification_check, customer_relationship, plus the cross-feature sync port interfaces (ScreeningPort, RiskPort, KycPort) and typed explanation shapes. No workflows, no vendor calls.

modules.name: screening
modules.responsibility: Shared list ingestion with versions and diffs (UN, OFAC SLS, EU FSF, UK FCDO, SAT 69-B), LATAM name normalisation and scoring, ScreeningIndex port usage, tenant-private encrypted lists (MX LPB), screening_run/screening_match/match_disposition/screening_whitelist, sync screen API, delta and periodic re-screening jobs, lists.events and screening.events. Implements core.ScreeningPort.

modules.name: risk
modules.responsibility: Versioned scorecard models and factor tables, deterministic evaluator with hard rules and bands, risk_assessment + factor rows, review-date computation, four-eyes overrides, simulate/activate with batch re-score, risk.events. Implements core.RiskPort; reads screening status from core read models, never imports screening.

modules.name: onboarding
modules.responsibility: KYC applications, journey generation from the effective policy, step workflow on WorkflowRun, capture sessions and uploads, connector checks via ConnectorRouter, identifier validators, assurance model A0-A4, decision ruleset with stable reason codes, review tasks, consent records, step-up/refresh, webhooks. Calls screening and risk through core ports (sync).

modules.name: kyb
modules.responsibility: Business applications, ownership declaration tree, party_relationship provenance, recursive effective-ownership engine, UBO determination per policy (25%, control, senior-manager fallback, total_fig_juridicas), reconciliation issues, registry snapshots (SAT CSF/RFC, 69-B via connectors), KYC sub-applications for reps and UBOs through core.KycPort, decision rules.

modules.name: monitoring
modules.responsibility: Canonical Txn schema, batch/file ingest with idempotency, enrichment (UDI/UMA/FIX, party resolution, counterparty hash), YAML rule DSL compiled to Python, bucketed window state in Postgres, async evaluation jobs, alerts with evidence, reportable_event capture per pack, tier limits, sync decide API, simulation over Postgres history, behaviour_profile snapshots. Publishes alerts.events and reportable.events; never imports cases or reporting.

modules.name: cases
modules.responsibility: Alert inbox (consumes alerts.events and screening.events by id), aml_case grouping, queues, visibility/ACL (RESTRICTED/INSIDER via extra RLS policy), country clocks from policy, four-eyes decisions, MX compliance committee sessions/votes/minutes, narrative templates, investigation workspace read models, MX freeze playbook as WorkflowRun, tenant webhooks (restriction/freeze/RFI). Emits case.events (incl. report requested).

modules.name: reporting
modules.responsibility: Report definition registry (versioned, valid_from/to), code-table service, report runs (period close, case-triggered drafts, zero reports), serializers (semicolon-delimited Formato 41, XML+XSD avisos) with character normalisers, business-rule validation, four-eyes approval, immutable artifact bytes + sha256 in object store, FilingChannel port (manual upload + receipt capture/parsing), corrections lifecycle, deadline dashboard. Reads reportable_event (monitoring) and case data (cases) through their public query functions; emits report.events.

modules.name: obligations
modules.responsibility: obligation_def seeds from packs, daily generator (13-month horizon, idempotent by def+period), DUE_SOON/LATE statuses and notifications, auto-evidence from report.events and review metrics, event-driven notices (officer/committee change), governance registries (compliance_officer_appointment, training_record, policy_document), board-pack export.

modules.name: sandbox
modules.responsibility: Deterministic magic identities per connector (e.g. CURP that returns REGISTRY_MISMATCH, INE timeout), mock connector implementations registered through the platform mock framework, seed personas and transaction streams for demo tenants, sandbox tenant provisioning. Only module allowed to know every feature's fixtures.

modules.name: app
modules.responsibility: Composition root: assembles FastAPI routers from every feature's api.py, wires port adapters from settings (postgres/local vs later adapters), worker entrypoint running OutboxDispatcher + job workers + cron, CLI (migrate, seed, lists sync, run-worker, verify-audit). Enforced as the only module that imports everything (import-linter contract in CI).

modules.name: frontend (console)
modules.responsibility: Analyst/compliance-officer console adapted from sentinel: typed client generated from OpenAPI, allowed_actions-driven UI, pages for alerts, cases, committee, screening review, onboarding review, KYB tree, report approval + download + receipt upload, obligations calendar, rule packs, audit verify, tenant admin (staff, API keys, LPB upload). Depends only on the HTTP API.

ports.name: EventBus (transactional outbox)
methods: publish(event: Event) -> None  # inserts outbox row in the caller's DB transaction
subscribe(event_type: str, handler: Callable[[Event], None]) -> None
dispatch_pending(batch: int = 200) -> int  # worker loop; FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, marks published_at
replay(tenant_id, since) -> Iterator[Event]
ports.mvp_adapter: PostgresOutboxBus: outbox table (10-f00 §7.1) + in-process OutboxDispatcher in the worker that invokes registered handlers inside their own transaction and records delivery in outbox_delivery (idempotent by event_id+handler).
ports.later_adapter: KafkaBus: Debezium or poller relay publishes outbox rows to Kafka topics (party.events, screening.events, alerts.events, case.events, report.events, lists.events); handlers become consumer groups keyed tenant_id:party_id. Same Event envelope, same handler signatures.

ports.name: JobQueue + WorkflowRunner
methods: enqueue(job_type, payload, run_at=None, idempotency_key=None, tenant_id=None) -> JobId
schedule_cron(name, cron_expr, job_type, payload) -> None
claim(worker_id, job_types) -> Job | None  # SKIP LOCKED, lease with heartbeat
complete(job_id) / fail(job_id, error, retry_in: timedelta | None) -> None
start_workflow(workflow_type, key, input) -> WorkflowRunId
signal(run_id, name, payload) -> None  # e.g. capture_submitted, review_decided
run_step(run_id) -> StepResult  # advances persisted state machine; steps are idempotent activities
wait_for(run_id, condition, timeout, then: str) -> None
ports.mvp_adapter: PostgresJobQueue (job table, exponential backoff, dead-letter after N attempts) + WorkflowRun table (workflow_type, key, state, step, context jsonb, wake_at, signals jsonb). Onboarding, KYB, re-screen, report runs, rescore and freeze playbooks are written as step functions driven by this runner.
ports.later_adapter: TemporalRunner: each workflow_type becomes a Temporal workflow and each step function an activity with the same signature; signals map 1:1; payload codec encrypts PII. Cron moves to Temporal schedules.

ports.name: ScreeningIndex
methods: index_list_version(list_version_id, entries: Iterable[IndexEntity]) -> None
index_private_list(tenant_id, private_list_id, entries) -> None
candidates(query: NameQuery, scope: IndexScope, top_k: int = 50) -> list[Candidate]  # retrieval only; scoring is Python
reverse_candidates(changed_entries: Iterable[IndexEntity], tenant_id) -> list[Candidate]  # delta rescreen against customer names
retire_list_version(list_version_id) -> None
stats() -> IndexStats
ports.mvp_adapter: InMemoryScreeningIndex: process-local structures rebuilt from Postgres on worker/api start (folded-name tokens, LATAM phonetic key buckets, blind-index ID map), rapidfuzz process.extract for blocking (sentinel matcher.py pattern), per-tenant private-list segments decrypted into memory on demand and evicted; customer-name index per tenant for reverse screening.
ports.later_adapter: OpenSearchIndex (ICU folding, beider_morse es/pt, edge n-grams, tenant-filtered aliases for private lists) or yente with custom-dataset manifests, per research tech-screening-reporting §D.7 and recommended pipeline.

ports.name: ObjectStore
methods: put(tenant_id, key, data: bytes, content_type, kind: Literal['document','biometric','evidence','artifact']) -> ObjectRef  # returns sha256
get(ref: ObjectRef) -> bytes
presign_put(tenant_id, key, content_type, ttl) -> UploadUrl
presign_get(ref, ttl) -> DownloadUrl
put_immutable(tenant_id, key, data, retain_until: date) -> ObjectRef  # WORM semantics
delete(ref) -> None  # refused when legal_hold or retain_until active
ports.mvp_adapter: LocalFsObjectStore under var/objects/<tenant_id>/<kind>/..., content encrypted with the tenant DEK (biometric kind uses the separate biometric DEK), sha256 recorded, immutability enforced by a manifest table; presigned URLs are short-lived signed API routes.
ports.later_adapter: S3ObjectStore with per-tenant prefixes, SSE-KMS per tenant key, Object Lock compliance mode for evidence/artifacts/audit anchors; GCS variant for cross-cloud DR (08-infrastructure §8 option C).

ports.name: KeyProvider
methods: generate_dek(tenant_id, purpose: Literal['data','biometric','index']) -> WrappedKey
unwrap(tenant_id, wrapped: WrappedKey) -> bytes  # cached 5 min in memory
hmac_key(tenant_id, purpose) -> bytes  # blind indexes
rotate(tenant_id, purpose) -> WrappedKey
destroy(tenant_id) -> None  # crypto-shredding, blocked by legal_hold
ports.mvp_adapter: LocalKeyProvider: one master key from env/file (AES-256-GCM) wraps per-tenant DEKs stored in tenant_key; same table schema and key hierarchy as production so only the wrapping call changes.
ports.later_adapter: AwsKmsKeyProvider: cell KMS key -> per-tenant KEK (KMS) -> wrapped DEKs; BYOK for large tenants; destroy = schedule KEK deletion.

ports.name: UnitValueFetcher
methods: fetch(unit_code: str, start: date, end: date) -> list[UnitValue]  # value, quote_ccy, source, fetched_at
supported_units() -> list[str]
ports.mvp_adapter: SeedFileFetcher reading policy-packs/shared/units/seed_*.yaml plus a console/CLI manual upload (unit_value rows are never overwritten; corrections chain via superseded_by). Missing dates raise UnitValueMissing and block threshold decisions, as in 10-f00 §5.
ports.later_adapter: BanxicoSieFetcher (UDI daily, FIX prior-banking-day rule), InegiUmaFetcher (annual, valid 1 Feb), run by cron jobs at 18:00 America/Mexico_City.

ports.name: Connector / ConnectorRouter / CredentialVault (vendor clients)
methods: Connector._call(req: ConnectorRequest, creds: Credentials) -> RawResponse
Connector._interpret(raw) -> CheckResult  # PASS/FAIL/INCONCLUSIVE + assurance_contrib
Connector.run(req, ctx) -> VerificationCheck  # retries, timeout, evidence put, cost meter
ConnectorRouter.route(check_type, country, tenant_id) -> list[Connector]  # primary -> fallback
CredentialVault.get(tenant_id, connector_name, mode: PLATFORM|TENANT) -> Credentials
ConnectorRegistry.register(name, factory, sandbox_factory) -> None
ports.mvp_adapter: Sandbox mock connectors for every MX check (DOC_AUTH, LIVENESS, FACE_MATCH_DOC, REGISTRY_ID:RENAPO_CURP, REGISTRY_BIOMETRIC:INE, TAX_ID:SAT_RFC, ACCOUNT_OWNERSHIP:CLABE, COMPANY_REGISTRY:SAT_CSF, FISCAL_LIST:SAT_69B) driven by magic identities, with realistic latency/outage simulation, evidence blobs and unit costs; CredentialVault backed by an encrypted tenant_secret table.
ports.later_adapter: IncodeConnector (doc+liveness+INE face/data), Nubarium/Kiban or Didit for RENAPO/SAT, NA-AT/Veridas as INE fallback, SEON/Incognia device risk, per research tech-idv-kyb-vendors MX matrix; CredentialVault moves to Secrets Manager/Vault paths per tenant.

ports.name: FilingChannel
methods: prepare(report_run_id) -> FilingPackage  # file bytes, filename, checksum, step-by-step instructions, portal URL
submit(package, creds: Credentials | None) -> FilingResult  # ACCEPTED/REJECTED/ERROR + regulator receipt ref
record_manual_receipt(filing_id, receipt: bytes, content_type) -> ReportFiling
parse_receipt(channel_code, receipt: bytes) -> Receipt  # folio, timestamp, record count, status
ports.mvp_adapter: ManualUploadChannel: compliance officer downloads the approved artifact, uploads it to CNBV SITI PLD/FT or SAT SPPLD under their own credentials/e.firma (never custodied), then uploads the acuse; parser extracts folio/timestamp from SITI acuse text and SAT acuse XML/PDF; status becomes FILED/ACKNOWLEDGED/REJECTED.
ports.later_adapter: SiscoafSoapChannel (BR, zeep + e-CPF signing), UafAutomatedChannel (CL, IP-whitelisted), optional Playwright portal helper where terms allow; same ReportFiling rows and receipts.

ports.name: Clock
methods: now() -> datetime  # tz-aware UTC
today(tz: str) -> date
is_business_day(country, scope, d: date) -> bool  # delegates to calendar
ports.mvp_adapter: SystemClock in app/worker; FrozenClock injected in golden tests (deadline rules, period closes, UMA year change on 1 Feb, FIX prior-banking-day).
ports.later_adapter: Unchanged; kept as a port so Temporal workflow time and replay stay deterministic.

ports.name: AuditSink
methods: append(tenant_id, event: AuditEvent) -> AuditEntry  # same DB transaction as the change; per-tenant chain
verify(tenant_id, from_id=None, to_id=None) -> ChainVerification
anchor(tenant_id) -> AnchorRef  # writes latest hash outside the DB
query(tenant_id, entity_type, entity_id, cursor) -> Page[AuditEntry]
ports.mvp_adapter: PostgresAuditSink: audit_event table with INSERT-only trigger (sentinel migration 0001 pattern), per-tenant hash chain with advisory lock keyed by tenant hash, nightly anchor job writing the head hash to ObjectStore.put_immutable.
ports.later_adapter: WormAuditSink: stream audit.events to S3 Object Lock (compliance mode) with searchable copy in ClickHouse/OpenSearch; chain per tenant per day with external timestamp anchoring.

ports.name: HotAggregateStore + TxnHistory (monitoring state)
methods: get_buckets(keys: list[AggKey], window: Window) -> dict[AggKey, list[Bucket]]
upsert_bucket(key, bucket_ts, delta: AggDelta) -> None
snapshot_for_sync(tenant_id, customer_id) -> SyncProfile  # hot aggregates + profile for decide API
history(tenant_id, filters, order=event_time) -> Iterator[Txn]  # simulation and investigation timeline
ports.mvp_adapter: Postgres txn_bucket table (hourly buckets <= 7d, daily <= 6m, calendar accumulators per period) keyed (tenant_id, key_type, key_hash, bucket_ts) plus monthly-partitioned transaction table; sync path reads a small in-process LRU warmed by the async worker.
ports.later_adapter: RedisHotAggregateStore for the <=100 ms decide path and ClickHouse TxnHistory for simulation/timeline (15-f05 §2.1, §6.2); bucket semantics and the rule engine stay identical.

ports.name: WebhookDelivery + Notifier
methods: enqueue_webhook(tenant_id, event_type, payload_refs) -> DeliveryId  # no PII, references only
deliver(delivery_id) -> DeliveryResult  # HMAC-SHA256 X-Signature/X-Timestamp, backoff 24h
notify(tenant_id, channel: EMAIL|SLACK, template, context) -> None
ports.mvp_adapter: Jobs-backed delivery with httpx; dead-letter rows visible in console; Notifier logs + SMTP stub (console inbox page shows notifications for demos).
ports.later_adapter: Dedicated webhook service consuming Kafka topics; SES/SendGrid and Slack/Teams adapters.

shared_core_model: tenant (id, legal_name, country_code, cell, env SANDBOX|PROD, status, created_at): root of every RLS policy; sandbox tenants are ordinary tenants with env=SANDBOX (08-infrastructure §10)
tenant_key (tenant_id, purpose data|biometric|index, version, wrapped_dek, created_at, destroyed_at): per-tenant DEKs behind KeyProvider; crypto-shredding target
tenant_policy (tenant_id, pack_version_id, overrides jsonb, effective_from, approved_by): which packs a tenant inherits and its only-tighten overrides
policy_pack / policy_pack_version (code, version, effective_from, config jsonb): shared rulebooks; no tenant_id
policy_snapshot (tenant_id, content_hash, content jsonb): frozen effective policy referenced by every decision record (10-f00 §4.4)
staff_user (tenant_id, sso_subject, email, roles[], active) + staff_credential for local login: analysts, MLRO, auditor read-only; drives app.user_id/app.user_roles
api_client / api_key (tenant_id, client_id, key_hash, scopes[], env, revoked_at): machine auth for the fintech's backend and webhooks
unit_value (unit_code, valid_from, valid_to, value, quote_ccy, source, fetched_at, superseded_by): effective-dated UMA/UDI/FIX; thresholds use the value on the transaction date
holiday (country, regulator_scope, date, name, source): business-day math for deadlines and clocks
party (tenant_id, party_type, country_code, retention_until, legal_hold) with person / organization: one party per tenant per human/company; never shared across tenants
party_identifier (tenant_id, party_id, id_type, value_enc, value_hash, verified_by): CURP/RFC/CLABE encrypted with blind index for dedup and exact list matching
party_address (tenant_id, party_id, address_type, address_enc, admin_area, municipality): geo risk at municipality level and report fields

party_relationship (tenant_id, from_party_id, to_party_id, rel_type, ownership_pct, control_basis, provenance, valid_from/to): ownership/control graph and PEP relatives, needed by KYB, screening and reporting
document (tenant_id, party_id, doc_type, storage_key, sha256, extracted jsonb, uploaded_at): evidence pointer shared by onboarding, KYB, cases and reports

verification_check (tenant_id, party_id, application_id, check_type, provider, credential_mode, result, score, assurance_contrib, response_ref, cost_minor, route, performed_at): immutable record of every external call; feeds evidence packs and metering
customer_relationship (tenant_id, party_id, external_ref, status, account_tier, current_risk_id, next_review_at, started_at, ended_at): the fintech's customer; idempotency anchor by external_ref

sentinel_reuse.how: Becomes src/kycaml/platform/audit/chain.py: keep AuditEvent, _digest canonical JSON, record() inside the caller's transaction and verify_chain(); add tenant_id, actor_type, entity scoping, a per-tenant advisory lock (hash of tenant_id) so tenants do not serialise each other, and an anchor() that writes the head hash to ObjectStore.put_immutable.
Copied into the first kycaml migration for audit_event; the same trigger pattern is reused as a template for INSERT-only tables (match_disposition, case_decision, report_artifact).

Seed of src/kycaml/screening/normalize/: keep strip_accents, tokens(), PARTICLES/HONORIFICS/LEGAL_SUFFIXES and reorder_list_name; extend per research §D.3 with particle tagging instead of dropping, suffix qualifiers, married-name variants, ES/BR structural variants, nickname expansion and the LATAM phonetic key.

Subject, Adjustment, MatchExplanation and ScreeningMatch shapes are kept as the explanation contract (console already renders them); the Screener's rapidfuzz process.extract blocking becomes InMemoryScreeningIndex.candidates(); the averaged token_set/token_sort score is replaced by the token-aligned IDF formula of research §D.4-D.6 but retained as a secondary feature so existing behaviour can be compared in shadow mode.

ListEntry/Identifier become the internal index entity model; parse_ofac is replaced by an OFAC SLS enhanced-XML parser (per research §A.1) but write_snapshot/load_snapshot and the gzip snapshot format are kept for offline tests and sandbox; the OpenSanctions PEP downloader is kept behind the licence flag.
Copied as-is to src/kycaml/screening/ingest/countries.py for OFAC remark country mapping.
Moved to tests/fixtures/lists/ for deterministic matcher tests and to the sandbox seed (fictional PEPs clearly labelled) until a PEP licence exists.

Becomes src/kycaml/onboarding/validators/identifiers.py: keep CURP regex/check digit/embedded DOB-sex-state cross-check, RFC person format and CPF/NIT helpers; add RFC homoclave mod-11, RFC 12-char persona moral and CLABE check digit; DocumentCheck shape feeds verification_check rows of check_type IDENTIFIER_FORMAT.

The six rule kinds (threshold, aggregate, structuring, velocity, high_risk_jurisdiction, profile_deviation) and Context.window semantics become the first compiled templates of the monitoring DSL in src/kycaml/monitoring/dsl/kinds.py; RuleHit maps to alert + alert_evidence; Money/FxTable are replaced by platform.units; Jurisdictions becomes the country_risk factor table.

RiskFactor and RiskAssessment remain the API/console explanation shapes in src/kycaml/risk; the additive pack-weight model is replaced by the scorecard evaluator from 14-f04, with sentinel's factors (sanctions match, PEP, FATF nationality, occupation, document validity, declared volume) re-expressed as factors/hard rules in MX-ITF-default v1.

Four-eyes checks (_require_second_reviewer, proposer != approver), MIN_RATIONALE_LENGTH, open_case grouping and the allowed_actions mirror pattern move to src/kycaml/cases/decisions.py and cases.py; the state machine is extended to 16-f06 §2.2 (PROPOSED_DECISION, COMMITTEE, REPORT_DRAFTING) and roles to ANALYST/SENIOR_ANALYST/MLRO/AUDITOR_RO/ADMIN.
Moved to src/kycaml/core/explanations.py; HitExplanation/AlertExplanation kept, ReportDraft replaced by reporting's typed run preview.

App factory (operation-id naming for generated clients, lifespan preloads, SPA mount), per-request session dependency and DomainError/NotFoundError/ForbiddenError become src/kycaml/platform/api/ with the error handler switched to RFC 9457 problem+json and the session wrapped with SET LOCAL tenant context.

pydantic-settings pattern, engine/sessionmaker, alembic upgrade helper and Typer CLI layout reused in platform/config.py, platform/db.py and app/cli.py (commands: db upgrade, seed-sandbox, lists sync, run-worker, audit verify).

Monitoring thresholds and Spanish rule names seed the MX typology rules in policy-packs/MX/ITF-IFPE/v1.yaml after re-mapping from DCG art. 115 LIC (bank) to DCG art. 58 LRITF (ITF: cash >= USD 5,000, FX cash >= USD 500) as the product-readiness page requires; _jurisdictions.yaml seeds the shared country_risk table.
Persona/Tx dataclasses and valid-check-digit generators become src/kycaml/sandbox/seed.py producing sandbox tenants, magic identities and transaction streams through the real services.

Testcontainers Postgres 17 session, savepoint-per-test session, TestClient with dependency override and typed parse/parse_list/error helpers are reused verbatim; added fixtures: two tenants, staff users per role, API keys, FrozenClock, and the isolation harness.

Toolchain (ruff ALL with the same ignores, ty, basedpyright all-strict, vulture, pytest cov >= 90, testcontainers) and the single-image build are copied; compose keeps only Postgres; a worker entrypoint is added.

sentinel_reuse.sentinel_path: frontend/ (whole app: src/api/client.ts, queries.ts, types.ts, schema.d.ts generation, components/ui, components/layout, features/cases, features/explain, features/audit, features/login, features/rules, features/screening, hooks, lib)
sentinel_reuse.how: Adopted as the console: openapi-fetch client with bearer middleware, TanStack queries, shadcn UI kit and AppShell kept; schema regenerated from kycaml OpenAPI (`npm run gen:api`); CaseDetailPage/ActionPanel/Timeline/RiskBreakdown/MatchBreakdown adapted to new payloads; new features added (alerts inbox, committee, onboarding-review, kyb, reporting, obligations, admin); strings moved to an es-MX i18n file; demo-login replaced by staff login.
Kept as the pattern for explaining missing actions: policyNote mirrors the backend allowed_actions for cases, report approvals and risk overrides.

Design trade-offs become ADR-0001..0005 in docs/adr (typed rule kinds vs DSL - superseded by the DSL decision; audit chain limits and anchoring; in-memory matcher scale ceiling and the ScreeningIndex port); Mermaid diagrams are regenerated per sub-project spec.

risks.risk: Solo-developer throughput: 37 estimated weeks against an 8-engineer plan and fixed regulatory dates (01-06-2027 new AV formats, 01-03-2027 BO/EBR chapters).
risks.mitigation: Pilot-first order so value is visible at P3/P5/P6; each sub-project ships its own spec, plan and golden tests so the agent can execute with less supervision; re-plan after every sub-project; keep P8-P10 scopes cuttable (hosted KYB app, board-pack PDF) without touching isolation primitives.

risks.risk: Report formats are built from public specs only; SITI PLD/FT QA and SAT SPPLD acceptance cannot be verified without a design partner, and FX-cash/TIF/VA UIF layouts are not obtained.
risks.mitigation: Golden files derived from the Formato 41 resolution and avi.xsd; a local validator that mirrors regulator rules; data for the unobtained layouts is captured in reportable_event so serializers can be added without re-ingest; partner test filing is a hard gate for pilot go (delivery plan T8.1).

risks.risk: Postgres-first adapters leak semantics into feature code, making the later swap to Kafka/Temporal/OpenSearch/Redis a rewrite.
risks.mitigation: Port contract test suites in tests/contracts run against every adapter; handlers idempotent by event_id; workflow steps written as pure activities with persisted context; import-linter forbids feature modules from importing adapter classes; a quarterly spike runs one contract suite against the later adapter.

risks.risk: In-memory screening index exceeds memory or startup time once PEP data (millions of entities) or many tenants' customer-name indexes are loaded.
risks.mitigation: Sanctions-only in memory at pilot (hundreds of thousands of names); PEP behind licence flag; per-tenant private/customer segments loaded lazily with eviction; OpenSearch adapter scheduled when PEP licence lands; index stats exposed for monitoring.

risks.risk: LATAM name-matching false-positive and false-negative rates are untested (no published benchmark).
risks.mitigation: Pair corpus from P1 grows to the P7 evaluation corpus with CI recall gate; sentinel scorer kept as a shadow feature for comparison; dispositions feed the labelled set; thresholds per list kind versioned in matcher_version and stored on every run.

risks.risk: RLS misconfiguration (table owner bypass, missing FORCE, pooled connection leaking app.tenant_id) silently breaks isolation.
risks.mitigation: Separate owner and runtime roles from P0; SET LOCAL per transaction; migration linter requires ENABLE+FORCE RLS and tenant_id NOT NULL on every tenant table; auto-discovered two-tenant harness in CI; composite (tenant_id,id) FKs completed in P11 before pilot.

risks.risk: Readable normalised names for fuzzy matching conflict with field-level encryption promises (07-data-model §9 rule 4 open decision).
risks.mitigation: Decide in P0 (recommended: full_name_norm plaintext tokens readable only by the matcher DB role; raw names encrypted; reverse-screen index built from those tokens); document in the DPA/security pack.

risks.risk: Mock connectors diverge from real vendor behaviour (latency, outages, score scales), so onboarding decision rules are tuned against fiction.
risks.mitigation: Connector contract tests with recorded fixtures per vendor once sandbox access exists; assurance-contribution model prevents silent downgrades; mocks simulate INE 5-7 s latency and outages; vendor adapters are additive behind ConnectorRouter.

risks.risk: The rule DSL compiler (YAML to Python AST, declared aggregates, bucketed state) becomes a multi-week rabbit hole.
risks.mitigation: Grammar v1 limited to what the MX typology library and captures need; sentinel's six kinds as first templates; compile to closures over a small evaluator rather than general AST; simulation reuses the same evaluator so there is one engine to debug.

risks.risk: Sync decision latency target (p99 <= 100 ms) may not be met on Postgres buckets.
risks.mitigation: Deferred to P11 and measured at pilot volume; HotAggregateStore port isolates the Redis swap; fail-open with REVIEW flag configurable so the partner's SPEI path never blocks on us.

risks.risk: Tenant credentials and e.firma handling: custody would create CFF Art. 17-J and SITI credential liability.
risks.mitigation: ManualUploadChannel only for Mexico; CredentialVault holds vendor credentials, never e.firma; receipts prove filing; documented in runbooks and contracts.

risks.risk: Modular monolith erodes into a tangle (feature modules importing each other), blocking later service extraction.
risks.mitigation: Layering enforced by import-linter contracts in CI (platform <- core <- features <- app); cross-feature sync calls only via core.ports; cross-feature async only via events with versioned types.

open_questions: Design-partner profile: consumer wallet/IFPE (SPEI, individuals) or B2B/SME fintech? If B2B, move P8 KYB ahead of P6 Formato 41 and add the hosted business onboarding app to P8 scope.

Normalised-name storage decision (07-data-model §9 rule 4): plaintext full_name_norm restricted to the matcher DB role (recommended) vs decrypt-into-memory per tenant; this must be fixed in P0 because it shapes the index and the DPA.
Sandbox topology: sandbox tenants as ordinary tenants with env=SANDBOX in the same cell database and RLS (recommended, cheapest) vs a separate sandbox database per environment.
Staff authentication for the pilot: local email/password + TOTP built in P0 with an OIDC adapter later (recommended for demos) vs OIDC-only against the partner's IdP from day one.
Transaction feed contract with the partner: all transactions or only above a floor, and whether daily balance snapshots are sent (needed for tier limits and structuring rules; 15-f05 §13).
Default sync-decision posture per rail (fail-open with REVIEW vs fail-closed) once P11 lands.

Sentinel licence: relicense the private repo from MIT to proprietary before its code is merged into kycaml (product-readiness page §9) — needed before any partner sees code or receives a self-hosted deployment.
PEP data before pilot: ship with UN/OFAC/EU/UK + tenant LPB only, or fund the OpenSanctions Reseller/OEM licence (or a per-query API) so PEP screening is live at pilot.
Console language: Spanish-first strings from P0 (small ongoing cost) vs English until the P11 pass; recommended Spanish-first since Valeria/Diego are the pilot users.

Pilot deployment target and residency commitment: single managed Postgres + container service in mx-central-1 (AWS) with encrypted in-country backups, or the partner's own cloud account; decides the ObjectStore/KeyProvider adapters needed before pilot and whether P11 includes S3/KMS adapters.

Policy default for domestic PEPs (HIGH floor, tenant may not lower in MX) and the N1 tier assurance (A1 + geolocation without liveness) — product owner sign-off needed for MX/ITF-IFPE v1 before P3 golden tests are frozen.
Scope of P6 UIF layouts: wait for the partner to supply FX-cash/TIF/VA layouts (ship ROR/ROI/24h/ROIP only) or invest in best-guess serializers behind a flag.
